title: Neighbourhood presentation of the strict-local derived mate
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ a geometric point, $g:S_{(s)}\to S$ its strict-henselization map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], $X'=X\times_S S_{(s)}$, $p:X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to S_{(s)}$. For every $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(X_{et}))$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, the map $m=\Gamma(S_{(s)},H^n(\mathrm{mate}_K))$ has a global cohomology continuity presentation with base $T=X$, object $K$, and degree $n$ [def-weil-pbc-global-cohomology-continuity-presentation]. The source cocone is colimiting and the composite of each source leg with $m$ is the canonical projection pullback. No target colimit or invertibility assertion is made.

source.place: Tags 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), 03Q8 and 0GIT; presentation of neighbourhood restriction maps

proof.text: Choose the small affine pointed-neighbourhood representative category from strictHenselization_properties. Its inclusion is initial and the representative diagram has the strict henselization as limit. Apply the fibre-product limit construction along f and identify its structural map using the prescribed affine legs. The stages are qcqs because f is qcqs and the neighbourhood bases are affine. Every transition is affine since it is the base change of a map between affine schemes. This gives I, D, c, t, p and their geometric properties.

Take F to be the neighbourhood hypercohomology diagram. Choose a bounded-below injective representative J of K. Restriction to an etale neighbourhood preserves injectives, so sections of its restriction compute hypercohomology. Functorial restriction of sections, under derived adjunction and Leray, yields the stated transition formula and its functor laws. Sheafification of this cohomology presheaf computes homology of Rf_*K. Stalk invariance under sheafification and initiality of affine representatives give a colimiting cocone with vertex the geometric stalk. The germ restriction is invertible and exact inverse image commutes with homology; transport this cocone to the source group of the displayed mate. This gives sourceLegs and sourceIsColimit, without using derived continuity.

Use exact strict-local global sections and the derived Leray comparison to identify the target with hypercohomology of the pullback limit. On J the adjunction mate restricts sections along the pullback square: a section over a neighbourhood is sent to its inverse-image section along the limit projection. Taking homology and expressing inverse-image composition by its canonical coherence isomorphism proves the restriction equation, for every source leg. These equations supply the presentation and do not assert that its target cocone is colimiting.
